themes.definition: Decisions were guided by whether the two versions truly mirrored each other and/or were balanced/mirror-like as a pair (e.g., not actually true mirrors, ensure mirror images and balance).
The influence/keep-remove decision emphasized factual backing/verifiability and penalized false, untrue, or misinformation-like content (sometimes contrasted with generic free-speech framing).

Evaluated whether the pair would support healthy, meaningful, or productive political conversation (often using uncertainty/fit/engagement checks, discouraging devolution, bashing-only, or dead ends).

themes.theme_label: Tone/language as a signal of aggression, incoherence, or “gibberish”
themes.definition: Used linguistic and format cues—arguing vs truth, anger vs sense, hurtful/aggressive/trolling, incoherence/all-caps gibberish, extreme/radicalized-sounding language—as grounds for removal or allowing.

The participant’s process was shaped by constraints that made pair-level removal/keeping mandatory (e.g., must delete both, can’t delete single items), sometimes leading to difficulty deciding, inability to justify removal, or defaulting to keeping both.
